title: Encountering wild animals in Poland
question: What should I do if I encounter a wild boar, fox or badger in Poland?
short_answer: Stay calm. Do not run, do not shout, do not feed. Back away slowly. Wild boars are increasingly common in Polish cities and parks.
conditions: 🐗 Wild boar (dzik): freeze, then back away slowly and quietly. Never run — it triggers a chase instinct
🦊 Fox (lis): keep distance. Urban foxes may carry rabies. Never touch or feed
🦡 Badger (borsuk): usually avoids humans. If it approaches you, back away calmly
Do not feed any wild animals — it makes them aggressive and dependent on humans
Wild boars are most active at dawn and dusk
If you see a wild animal acting strangely (disoriented, not afraid), call 112 or a vet
exceptions: Female boar with piglets (locha z prosiętami) is extremely dangerous — never get between them
A fox or badger that approaches humans without fear may have rabies — do not touch, call 112
Injured wildlife: contact RDOŚ (Regional Directorate for Environmental Protection)
penalties: Feeding wild animals in national parks: fine up to 500 PLN
Disturbing or harming protected species: fine up to 5000 PLN

sources.title: RDOŚ – Regional Directorate for Environmental Protection
